sources.document: Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults: An Overview of Reviews
sources.notes: The 2026 Position Stand reports strength benefits with heavier loads (≥80% 1RM) for 2–3 sets, and hypertrophy benefits with higher weekly volume (≥10 sets/week). It does not validate every TrainMind session-level range below.

sources.document: WHO Guidelines on Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour
sources.notes: Public-health weekly activity recommendations, not an individualized single-session prescription.
Exercise identity and source metadata only; not prescription methodology.
Product defaults are explicitly heuristics and do not claim exercise-science consensus.

rules.statement: For healthy adults, strength was enhanced by heavier loads (at least 80% 1RM) performed for 2–3 sets.
rules.notes: TrainMind uses the set range when the goal is strength. It does not invent an 1RM or convert an unknown load to 80%.

rules.statement: Hypertrophy was enhanced by higher resistance-training volume, with at least 10 sets per week as the highlighted threshold.
rules.notes: FROZEN 2026-11-10 — computed but never applied to scheduling. The source states weekly volume per muscle group / total body; this registry applies it per movement pattern, so the unit does not match (legs = squat + hinge + lunge would mean 30 sets/week). Scheduling uses the muscle-group rules instead (24h minimum interval, 2-3 sessions per week). Do not wire this field into dose allocation before unifying to a per-muscle framework and re-verifying the source. Original note: movement-pattern volume is only an imperfect proxy for muscle-group volume; it is not treated as a single-session 10-set prescription.

rules.statement: Adults should accumulate 150–300 minutes of moderate aerobic activity or equivalent weekly activity and perform muscle-strengthening activity for all major muscle groups on at least 2 days per week.
rules.notes: This is long-term context. Current workout generation does not infer a weekly schedule from it.

rules.statement: Allocate a conservative number of sets per selected exercise according to experience, history, recovery, and the hard session-time limit.
rules.notes: Exact session set allocation and duration caps are product rules, not a direct numeric recommendation from ACSM or WHO.

rules.statement: Use goal-specific rep, rest, and effort ranges as adjustable starting points; never infer an unmeasured 1RM.
rules.notes: Specific defaults are product calibrations and need user outcome data.

rules.statement: Reduce planned volume when the user reports fatigue or recent high movement-pattern volume.
rules.notes: Exact reductions and recent-load thresholds are product heuristics.

rules.statement: Only progress after repeated successful exposure; regress or maintain after hard, failed, interrupted, or painful sets.
rules.notes: Evidence counts and adjustment steps are product rules. Pain remains a Safety Gate concern and is never treated as ordinary difficulty.

rules.statement: Estimate exercise and compatible movement capability from recent completed performance, confidence, effort feedback, pain, staleness, and interruption evidence; adjust one dose variable at a time within knowledge and session limits.
rules.notes: Confidence bands, 30/90-day staleness, one-rep steps, hysteresis, and cross-exercise compatibility rules are deterministic product heuristics, not physiological predictions. Capability transfers never copy load.

rules.statement: Resolve goal-specific required movement stimulus before selecting exercises that satisfy it.
rules.notes: Pattern allocations are deterministic product mappings, not clinical prescriptions.

rules.statement: Estimated required session duration must not exceed the user's stated maximum; remove lower-priority volume or movements before reducing rest assumptions.
